repo.description: 🌐 Human-friendly and powerful HTTP request library for Node.js

checks.title: Repo description
checks.detail: “🌐 Human-friendly and powerful HTTP request library for Node.js” (63 chars)
checks.fix: Write a 15–130 char description: what it does + for whom + the differentiator.

checks.title: Topics (3+)
checks.detail: http, http-client, http-request, https, nodejs, npm-package
checks.fix: Add 3–8 topics mixing domain (cli, api) and ecosystem (nodejs, rust). They drive GitHub search & topic pages.

checks.title: Homepage URL
checks.detail: No homepage URL in the About sidebar.
checks.fix: Set the repo homepage (docs site, demo, or README anchor) — it is the only clickable field in the About box.

checks.title: Hero image / GIF above the fold
checks.fix: Put a screenshot/GIF/demo within the first ~40 lines. Visitors decide in seconds; text alone rarely converts.

checks.title: Install command near the top
checks.fix: Move the copy-paste install one-liner into the first screen of the README (top ~60 lines).

checks.title: Badges (1–12)
checks.fix: Add 3–5 badges (build, npm/pypi version, license). They signal “this is maintained”.

checks.title: Repo name quality
checks.fix: Pick a memorable, searchable name: 3–24 chars, hint at what it does, avoid test/demo/tmp prefixes.

checks.title: Copy-paste install command
checks.fix: Add an obvious one-liner: `npm i your-pkg` / `pip install your-pkg` / `cargo add ...`. This single line is the #1 conversion lever.

checks.title: Quickstart code block
checks.fix: Add a “Quick start” section with a runnable snippet near the top — show the happy path in < 10 lines.

checks.title: Examples / docs directory
checks.fix: Add an examples/ folder with 1–3 minimal runnable cases. Browsers of code trust examples.

checks.title: Package manifest at root
checks.detail: Found a package manifest (package.json, pyproject.toml, Cargo.toml, …).
checks.fix: Keep the ecosystem manifest (package.json / pyproject.toml / Cargo.toml / go.mod) at the repo root so tools and humans recognize the stack instantly.

checks.title: Docs / guide pointer
checks.fix: Link fuller docs (wiki, docs site, or ./docs) from the top of the README.

checks.title: License
checks.fix: Name the license in the README (e.g. “Licensed under GPL-2.0”) so adopters don’t have to guess.

checks.title: Tests detected
checks.detail: Found a test directory at the root.
checks.fix: Make existing tests discoverable: a root-level tests/ dir or test-runner config, and a CI badge.

checks.title: CI configured
checks.fix: Add a CI workflow (build + test) and show its badge at the top of the README.

checks.title: Recent activity (90d)
checks.fix: Keep a heartbeat: even small merged PRs keep the repo looking alive.

checks.title: Releases / tags
checks.fix: Publish a GitHub Release with readable notes. Releases trigger watcher emails and look maintained.

checks.title: Contributors (2+)
checks.fix: Invite contributions: label issues as “good first issue”, and list contributors in the README.

checks.title: Semver tags
checks.fix: Tag versions as v1.2 (or v1.2.3). Consistent version tags communicate stability to humans and package managers.

checks.title: Issue template
checks.detail: Found in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE (not surfaced by the community profile).
checks.fix: Add .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE with bug + feature forms. Triage cost drops, signal rises.

checks.title: PR template
checks.fix: Add a short PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md (what/why/how tested).

checks.title: CONTRIBUTING guide
checks.fix: Add CONTRIBUTING.md: how to set up dev env, run tests, and open a PR. Lower the barrier and outsiders appear.

checks.title: Discussions enabled
checks.fix: Enable Discussions and add an ideas/pinned welcome post. It gives shy users a place to land.

checks.title: Code of conduct
checks.fix: Add a CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md (GitHub provides a template in one click).

checks.title: Security policy
checks.detail: No SECURITY.md — the Security tab shows “no policy”.
checks.fix: Add SECURITY.md describing how to report vulnerabilities privately (GitHub: Settings → Security → private vulnerability reporting).

checks.title: Not a fork / not archived
checks.fix: If you intend to stop maintaining, say so in the README instead of archiving silently.

checks.title: README depth (50–1200 lines)
checks.fix: Too long: move details into docs/ and keep the README to one screen of decision-making info.

checks.title: README title matches repo name
checks.fix: Start the README with “# <repo-name> — one-line pitch”. Exact-name headings win browser tabs, search, and screenshots.

checks.title: Clear primary language
checks.fix: A detected primary language puts you in language topic pages and enables peer benchmarking.

checks.title: Stars in the last 28 days
checks.detail: Events feed shows ≥20 star(s) recently (lower bound; timestamps not paged).
checks.fix: Every push/announcement should ride a channel: Show HN, r/SideProject, dev communities, or a “what changed” post. Star velocity follows exposure.

checks.title: Stars per week (recent)
checks.fix: If velocity is near zero, treat the README as a landing page and re-launch the project (rename, rewrite the pitch, post again).
